recipes.name: Baked Cod with Boursin Herb Cheese
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) package Boursin cheese with herbs, room temperature
1 (14.5 ounce) can diced tomatoes with garlic, onion, and peppers, drained
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Pour 1 tablespoon melted butter into baking dish to coat bottom. Arrange the cod fillets in the dish. Pat fillets dry using a paper towel. Spread the Boursin cheese evenly over the fillets. Pour the tomatoes over the tops. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese. Drizzle with remaining 1 tablespoon butter.
Bake, uncovered, in preheated oven for 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Cod with Boursin Herb Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Bake cod fillets with a savory topping of herbed Boursin cheese, diced tomatoes seasoned with garlic, onions, and peppers, and Parmesan cheese, and enjoy a fast and easy seafood dish.

video.description: Use Boursin or Allouette Cheese and canned tomatoes seasoned with onion, peppers, and garlic to make this dish with fresh cod. It's an outstanding fish recipe for a quick and easy-to-prepare dinner.
video.name: How to Make Baked Cod with Boursin Herb Cheese

review.reviewBody:
This recipe was fantastic. Even my sometimes critical husband (who doesn't even really like fish) raved about it. I did make some minor changes however. I had no "spiced" tomatoes so I used canned diced tomatoes and sauted 3 cloves of garlic, 1 small onion finely chopped, and 1 small red pepper diced. I added the saute mixture to the tomatoes and put ove r the Boursin mixture. To all who want to save calories, spray baking dish with Pam and use a light herbed cream cheese (
Boursin is not necessary)!!! Will add to my regular rotation!

These are the small changes I made. Used mahi mahi instead of cod, diced up a red pepper and mixed with the Boursin, seasoned the fish liberally before spreading the Boursin then added a can of drained Italian seasoned tomatoes followed by light parm and dried parsley. Served with garlic quinoa with wilted spinach. Very very delicious and easy!! It’s an 11/10 in my opinion

I made this with beating egg white to stiff peek then folding in Herb whipped cream cheese (less expensive) Putting melted butter on the fish first, tenting with tinfoil while baking. Changed up just a little. Turned out good enough to fix for company, and will :)

This is especially good and easy. I made the sauce with green pepper, onion and garlic and a can of diced tomatoes sauteed about 8 minutes. Didn't have Boursin so I used cream cheese. I think most any cheese would work but I will try mozzarella next time even tho the cream cheese was delicious. Added just a hint of other spices like chili powder and celery salt . The fish had an excellent flavor, it was moist and looked attractive on the plate. I'm adding this to my 5 Star recipe book to be made again and again.

This was very good. I did only use half the butter and 3/4 of the block of cheese. I skipped the par meson, since I didn't have any. I also used fresh tomato's, half of a chopped onion and half a jalapeno (Can't bear to buy canned when there are so many tomatoes coming from the garden). I sautéed them for a few minutes before adding them to the fish. Super delicious. It is an expensive meal with the chees and the fish but worth it!

Great recipe. Very delish. I used goat cheese and sautéed the onion garlic and red pepper to add to diced tomatoes I think that might be better than a can if you have time. I cooked 25 mins then broiled on high for 3 mins. Perfect!!!
I like this recipe, but I also add black beans( canned and seasoned), and cover the cod afterwards with shaved parmigiana cheese and bake it for thirty minutes.

This recipe was amazing!!! The fish was tender and flaky and the topping was very rich and flavorful. I didn’t have canned tomatoes on hand. So I diced a tomato, half an onion and sautéed it in butter with some prepared garlic in the squeeze bottle and let that be my topping and it was out of this world. Husband told me I can make this anytime!!!

This was delicious. I used low fat Allouette cheese. Rather than canned tomatoes, I chopped up a tomato and 2 green onions. I sautéed them with chopped garlic and a little olive oil before putting them on top. Used spray rather than butter. Followed the rest of the recipe. Our cod did not take 40 minutes to cook but rather 25 minutes.

Yes, I used fresh tomatoes & garlic, salt & pepper
on top off the boursin cheese. Then put the melted
butter over the top That way I had a healthy dish.

Well this was a hit for us last night! I skipped the butter altogether and just sprayed my pan with vegetable cooking spray. I subbed tilapia for the cod and since I was making just two servings, I used an entire can of Rotel, well drained, but I reserved the juice. The Rotel gave this a nice kick. As previously suggested I used Herb Cheese Spread by lutzflcat, also on this site, for the Boursin cheese. I prepped this early in the afternoon, spreading the cheese spread thinly, covered and refrigerated until time to bake. I uncovered it, topped with tomatoes, salt and pepper, and just a little of the reserved juice to remoisten the tomatoes a little, and lastly the Parmesan. At this point I was going to drizzle a little butter over the top as indicated, but I forgot. My tilapia was much smaller than the amount listed in the recipe, so mine was perfectly cooked in 20 minutes. The only changes I would make next time would be to slightly increase the cheese spread (I was pretty skimpy with it this time), and I will try to remember the drizzle of butter over the top. This was very nice and Hubs said it’s a do over for sure!
Loved it have made several times but it is "soupy" lots of liquid in the pan, maybe I should drain the tomatoes ? Suggestions ?
I added cherry tomatoes from the garden. It added a pop of flavor.
This was an easy and delicious dish. I forgot to drizzle the butter over the top but I felt it really didn't need it. Thanks for a great recipe. I'll be making it again and again.
Very easy, quick and flavourful; you'll want to save this recipe.

This is a definite keeper. All I did different was to roughly chop some tomatoes, onions & garlic. Added some salsa, drained with a little bit of cilantro. Everyone loved it. I couldn’t take a picture because they wolfed it down as soon as it came out of the oven…🤗

This super easy recipe has become a family favorite, served with brown rice. My Costco regularly sells fresh cod and Boursin cheese. I can whip this together, put it in the oven in less than 10 minutes, and look like I've really done something.
Easy and company worthy
Normally not a fan of red sauce on fish, but the was delicious. All guest a seconds. Served over rice and added a pepper to the tomato mixture.
We used sea bass and OMG, it was so so so good. I have made it several times.
